body.estimand_functional: \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\) identifies the causal matrix and \(U=\operatorname{left}_r(M)\) is its row subspace.  The recorded estimator is \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}=\operatorname{left}_r(\mathcal P_r(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}))\) with \(\sup_P E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)\le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\).  The observed-data hybrid \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) reports \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\) when \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\) and the deterministic sine frame otherwise, and satisfies \(\sup_P E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\).  The causal target, the two estimators, and their risk bounds are distinct objects.

sampling_model.design: A triangular array of sequential randomized decisions ordered globally by \(o(i,j)=(i-1)m+j\), with filtration \((\mathbb G_k)_{k=0}^{nm}\) and explicit row baselines \(\mathcal F_{i,0}=\mathbb G_{(i-1)m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) units observed at \(m\) ordered decision times, with bounded aspect ratio; the sharp experiment and Markov witness use \(n_\ell=2\ell\) and \(m_\ell=2\lceil\gamma\ell\rceil\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A_{ij}\) is drawn with \(p_{ij}\in[q,1-q]\) given the global pre-cell field \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW--SVD uses the known predictable propensities and requires no estimated treatment nuisance.  Its expected-risk guarantee follows from bounded matrix-martingale concentration and a deterministic singular-subspace bound.  The blind procedure replaces entrywise propensities by a clipped empirical row fraction; propensity-path stability and the primitive oracle gap control its tangent expansion only at the explicit \(d_{nm}\) resolution.  The observed discrepancy compares blind and recorded fits at that same resolution and is not advertised as a \(b_{nm}\)-scale certificate.  Simultaneous bands use the direct recorded-IPW contrast and deterministic variance envelopes; leave-one-cell-out residuals and multiplier studentization are not needed for the conservative coverage theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Published Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, gives the rowwise upper bound, and Theorem 2, equation (22b) on page 953, gives the minimax lower bound under independent Bernoulli observation and independent noise.
Published Theorem 2.2 on page 1974 gives a Frobenius online-SGD rate and Theorem 3.1 on page 1977 gives fixed-form asymptotic normality for scalar rewards from independent Gaussian matrix contexts.
Published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 bound nearest-neighbor error for each unit-by-time counterfactual mean under an adaptive pooled sequential policy.

Published Theorem 2 and equation (14) on page 1724 give a Frobenius RMSE upper bound for nuclear-norm completion of an untreated potential-outcome matrix when adoption dates are independent across units conditional on the latent matrix.

Published Theorem 3 in Section 4 of article e70002 gives a restricted-strong-convexity and Frobenius-error guarantee for the low-rank term estimated by the weighted MAR objective in equations (2) and (11).
Published Propositions 1--3 develop tall-wide factor imputation rates and limit laws for missing common components, with average and individual treatment effects on the treated as applications.

The published COLT extended abstract on pages 3821--3822 and its public full version give entrywise consistency and asymptotic normality for synthetic nearest neighbors under causal missing-not-at-random sampling.

Published Theorem 5 on page 2021 compares Frobenius upper bounds for known-propensity IPW and uniform-risk nuclear-norm completion under independent Bernoulli observation with a low-rank probability matrix.
The published article and its public full version develop groupwise nuclear-norm completion and debiased asymptotic normality for fixed block or staggered missing-not-at-random causal panels.

Public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 give an armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD upper bound under independent Bernoulli assignments and low-rank arm means.  Only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{1/n+n/m^2}\) is shared: their rowwise matrix-error theorem has its own \(\log^4\) factor, whereas \(b_{nm}\) also has \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\) conversion to normalized effect-subspace loss.
Published Theorem 3 and equation (10) on page 7 characterize variance improvement for a scalar adaptively normalized IPW estimator under independent treatment indicators.
Predictably weighted adaptive IPW scores yield scalar studentized martingale limits.
Balancing weights attain Frobenius guarantees and a lower bound under fixed heterogeneous missingness.
Debiased low-rank projection yields inference for a fixed linear form under independent sampling.

ArXiv Assumption 2 on pages 7--8 gives normalized third-moment, predictable-covariance, empirical-covariance, plug-in, growth, and variance-floor conditions under which Theorem 3.3 on page 8 validates simultaneous multiplier intervals for many martingale means.
Published Theorem 4 and equation (14) on page 348 validate a multiplier maximum for a coefficient matrix under modeled nonuniform missingness.

body.tldr: Recorded propensities identify the causal effect matrix and make the entrywise IPW errors a bounded row-major martingale difference array.  On the frozen predictable class the strongest common-risk statement is the honest bracket \(c b_{nm}\le\inf_{\widetilde U}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)]\le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\).  Thus \(b_{nm}\) is a minimax lower/reference scale, not a matched frontier.  The endogenous-target construction rules out uniform \(b_{nm}\)-attainment by recorded IPW--SVD only; whether another observed-data estimator closes the bracket remains open.  Blind row scaling is certified only at the explicit \(d_{nm}\) resolution: both its causal loss and its observed disagreement differ from total drift by \(O_P(d_{nm})\).  With fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\), bounded aspect ratio, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), one has \(d_{nm}/b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt n\), so no \(b_{nm}\)-scale iff is claimed.  The rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law remains an explicit failure witness for blind scaling and a HeartSteps II stress design.  For predeclared dense families, direct finite-sample bands have a separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) multiplicity cost and make no feasible-multiplier exactness claim.

project_justification.gap: Published independent-mask rowwise matrix results do not settle causal effect-subspace risk under history-predictable assignment.  On the present effect-only low-rank class, a constant-propensity packing yields the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\), while a matrix-Freedman and deterministic subspace argument yields only \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) for recorded IPW--SVD.  The accepted endogenous-target example prevents labeling the latter estimator as \(b_{nm}\)-optimal, but it does not prove an estimator-independent lower bound above \(b_{nm}\).
project_justification.niche: The contribution is an explicit same-loss minimax bracket for a causal row subspace under predictable masks, together with an estimator-specific obstruction, a calibrated blind-normalization resolution theorem, and conservative simultaneous causal-contrast bands whose entropy cost is kept separate from the subspace scales.
project_justification.fill: The project proves an expected normalized maximum-row upper bound for recorded IPW--SVD, combines it with the constant-propensity minimax lower bound in one risk criterion, and records the remaining rate gap.  It proves two unconditional \(d_{nm}\)-resolution inequalities for blind scaling and shows algebraically that the former \(d_{nm}=O(b_{nm})\) premise is unavailable in the fixed-complexity \(b_{nm}=o(1)\) regime.  It also supplies the explicit Markov witness and a direct finite-sample union-bound band with separate family-size inflation.

body.related_work:
Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis are the closest rowwise estimator comparator: their public Algorithm 1, Theorem 3.2, and Corollary 3.3 analyze separate empirical-row-scaled SVD fits for two low-rank arm means under independent Bernoulli assignment.  Their geometric rowwise matrix-error scale motivates \(b^0_{nm}\), but their theorem does not cover history-predictable masks, effect-only low rank, the effect matrix's left singular space, or the present minimax criterion.  Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen prove two-to-infinity upper and lower bounds for an independently sampled low-rank matrix with independent noise; those results inform the deterministic perturbation and local packing architecture but do not make the causal target predictable under the row-major filtration.  The present result is therefore an honest bracket rather than a claimed matched extension of either paper.

Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey support the recorded-propensity martingale-score reduction, and Tropp supplies the bounded-increment matrix Freedman inequality used for the upper moment bound.  Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah study adaptive nearest-neighbor estimation of unit-by-time arm means under an exogenous factor model, a different target and structural class.  Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi; Sun, Zhu, and Dubin; Bai and Ng; Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen; Choi and Yuan; Mao, Wong, and Chen; and Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan address outcome completion, treatment effects on treated cells, entrywise or Frobenius loss, or fixed missingness structures.  None supplies the missing estimator-independent upper rate for the present predictable effect-subspace class, and the current effect-only rank condition does not imply their outcome-matrix assumptions.

Khan and Ugander analyze scalar affine normalization under independent indicators; the blind row-fraction SVD and its \(0.25/0.75\) Markov witness are new objects here and do not refute that published procedure.  Belloni and Oliveira and Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu motivate high-dimensional martingale or multiplier inference, but the retained simultaneous theorem uses direct finite-sample Freedman radii and a union bound only.  Its \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) factor is a query-family entropy cost, not part of either subspace scale.  Spruijt-Metz et al. make saved propensities and omission sensitivity operationally relevant for the HeartSteps II consumer.

body.technical_internal_limitation: Operator-norm martingale concentration followed by a deterministic subspace inequality pays the factor \(\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\), producing \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\).  The frozen class permits the target singular factors to depend on earlier outcomes, so the usual leave-one-row argument cannot simply treat those factors as predictable; the explicit obstruction shows that this is substantive for IPW--SVD.  The minimax lower scale \(b_{nm}\) therefore remains separated from the available upper rate.  For blind normalization, the ratio residual and stochastic spectral perturbation give resolution \(d_{nm}\); at fixed complexity and bounded aspect ratio, \(d_{nm}/b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt n\) whenever \(b_{nm}=o(1)\).  The separate arm means in the denominator derivative are not estimable at a claimed frontier rate under the current effect-only low-rank assumptions.  No residual covariance consistency, positive random studentizer, or feasible multiplier exactness is assumed or claimed.
body.honest_scope: Identification is given by the recorded IPW conditional mean.  The proved statistical statement is the expected-risk bracket between the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\) and the loose IPW--SVD radius \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\); these rates are not claimed to match.  The adaptive endogenous-target construction refutes only uniform \(b_{nm}\)-attainment by the specified IPW--SVD estimator.  It does not show that every estimator measurable from \(A,Y,p\) fails at that scale, so minimax tightness and the sharp constant remain open.  The blind procedure is introduced here and is certified only up to \(d_{nm}\); no unconditional \(b_{nm}\)-scale validity criterion or feasible tangent correction is claimed.  The \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is a boundary example for that procedure, not a refutation of a published method.  Simultaneous inference is supplied by conservative finite-sample direct-IPW radii, not by asymptotic exactness of the frozen leave-one-cell-out multiplier statistic.
